_note: Meat and cheese pairing chart (15 Nov 2026). Families of cured meat (rows) x families of cheese (cols). score: 3 classic, 2 good, 1 works with a sweet bridge, 0 skip. why: one short line in our own words. Proven pairs come from the ingredient pages at build time.

meats.name: Dry-cured ham
meats.line: Silky, sweet and salty. Easy to overpower, so it likes cheeses that are creamy or nutty rather than loud.

meats.name: Mild salami
meats.line: Garlicky, fatty and chewy. The most flexible meat on the board.

meats.name: Spicy salami & chorizo
meats.line: Chili heat and paprika. Wants a cool, creamy cheese to calm it, or a firm one that can stand up to it.
meats.q: What cheese goes with pepperoni and chorizo?

meats.name: Smoked sausage
meats.line: Smoky, tangy and a little sweet. Made for mild, melty cheeses and sharp cheddar.
meats.q: What cheese goes with summer sausage?

meats.name: Cooked ham & deli
meats.line: Tender, mild and sweet. Goes with almost any sliceable cheese, best with Swiss-style ones.
meats.q: What cheese goes with ham, mortadella and turkey?

meats.name: Air-dried beef
meats.line: Lean, deep red and beefy. Needs a cheese that adds the fat it lacks.

fresh: Cool milk against silky salt. Prosciutto with burrata is the Italian summer classic.
bloomy: Two gentle textures. Fine together, better with a fig jam or pear in between.
goat: Chèvre's tang lifts the ham's sweetness. Roll them together for an easy bite.
semi: Mild and melty works, but the cheese can make delicate ham taste flat.
alpine: Nutty and sweet together. Speck with a mountain cheese is a natural match.
aged: Same region, same long ageing: Parma ham with Parmigiano, jamón with manchego.
blue: Blue drowns delicate ham. Use a mild gorgonzola dolce and add honey or melon.

fresh: Fresh mozzarella cools a garlicky salami. The antipasto platter pairing.
bloomy: Salty salami against buttery brie. Rich, so keep the slices thin.
goat: Goat cheese's tang cuts through the salami's fat.
semi: Salami and provolone, salami and havarti: the deli pairing that never misses.
alpine: Gruyère's nuttiness is good with saucisson. The French way to do it.
aged: Firm with firm and salt with salt: aged cheddar, manchego or parm all work.
blue: Two strong, salty things. Works with a sweet bridge like fig jam or honey.

fresh: Cool, milky cheese puts out the fire. Burrata with nduja, mozzarella with pepperoni.
bloomy: Brie's cream softens chili heat, though the subtle rind gets lost.
goat: Tangy goat cheese cools spice and adds a bright edge.
semi: Provolone, pepper jack or havarti: pizza-shop logic, and it works.
alpine: Chili heat flattens the nutty notes you pay for in good Gruyère.
aged: Chorizo with manchego is Spain's tapas pair; firm cheese stands up to paprika.
blue: Hot salami and a strong blue are too much. Use sweet (mild) soppressata, a creamy blue, and honey or pear between them.

fresh: Smoke overpowers fresh cheese. Fine on a kids' board, not a standout.
bloomy: Smoke and a mushroomy rind clash a bit. Add pepper jelly to bridge them.
goat: Smoky and tangy pull apart. A sweet jelly helps.
semi: Summer sausage with colby jack or young gouda: the gift-box classic.
alpine: Swiss-style cheese with smoked sausage is a solid tailgate pair.
aged: Sharp cheddar meets tangy, smoky sausage. Add mustard and you're done.
blue: Smoke and blue both shout. A drizzle of honey makes it work.

fresh: Mortadella with burrata or ricotta is a popular Italian pairing. Soft on soft.
bloomy: Ham and brie: the French sandwich, minus the baguette.
goat: Mild meat and tangy cheese don't add much to each other.
semi: Ham and Swiss, turkey and havarti: mild with mild, and always eaten.
alpine: Sweet cooked ham and nutty Gruyère: a croque monsieur on a cracker.
aged: Ham with sharp cheddar works. The cheese leads, the ham supports.
blue: Blue overwhelms mild ham. Works with pear or apple in the bite.

fresh: Lean beef needs fat, and fresh cheese brings it.
bloomy: Creamy brie fills in what lean bresaola lacks.
goat: Bresaola rolled around goat cheese is a common Italian appetizer.
semi: Fine together, if not exciting. Add arugula and lemon.
alpine: Bündnerfleisch with a mountain cheese: same Alpine valleys.
aged: Bresaola with shaved Parmigiano, lemon and olive oil: the Lombardy plate.
blue: Beef and blue is a steakhouse pairing, and it works cured too.
